descriptions:
Hidden Marrakech with a local guide: a day for travellers who have seen the big sights, or simply want to go beyond them, discovering the quieter, older and more personal side of the city.

Start in the Mellah, the Jewish quarter founded in the 16th century next to the royal palace. With your guide, walk through its narrow lanes and spice market, visit the Lazama synagogue and see the old Jewish cemetery, with its rows of white tombs, one of the largest in Morocco. Your guide tells the story of the communities who lived here for centuries and of their role in the city's trade and crafts.

Then visit Dar Si Said, a 19th-century palace that now houses a museum of Moroccan woodwork, carpets and crafts, quiet and rarely crowded. After lunch in a riad restaurant, see the Almoravid Koubba, a small 12th-century domed pavilion and the only Almoravid monument left in the city, and Le Jardin Secret, a riad garden restored in 2016 with an Islamic garden, an exotic garden and a tower with views over the rooftops. Finish at the Menara gardens, where an old pavilion stands beside a great basin of water with the Atlas mountains behind it, especially beautiful in the late-afternoon light.

SCHEDULE (times are estimates)
11:00 – The Mellah and spice market
12:00 – Dar Si Said museum
13:00 – Lunch (not included)
14:30 – Almoravid Koubba
15:15 – Le Jardin Secret
16:30 – Menara gardens
17:30 – Drop-off

GOOD TO KNOW
• The Mellah was Marrakech's Jewish quarter, founded in the 16th century; your guide shows the Lazama synagogue and the old cemetery.
• Dar Si Said is a museum of Moroccan woodwork and crafts in a 19th-century palace.
• Le Jardin Secret was restored in 2016 and has an Islamic garden and an exotic garden.
• Modest dress (shoulders and knees covered) is appreciated at the synagogue and cemetery.

INCLUDED: licensed guide, private driver, pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: entrance fees, lunch, tips.

WHAT YOU'LL TASTE
Spices in the Mellah market and lunch at a riad restaurant.

PHOTO SPOTS
• The Koubba's carved dome.
• The tower view at Le Jardin Secret.
• The Menara pavilion with the Atlas behind.

ACCESSIBILITY
Flat routes; the car is used between distant sites.

WHAT YOU TAKE AWAY: The other Marrakech.

faq.question: Is this tour for repeat visitors?
faq.answer: Yes, and for anyone curious. It avoids the busiest monuments and shows quieter places most visitors miss: the Mellah, Dar Si Said, the Almoravid Koubba, Le Jardin Secret and the Menara gardens. If it's your first visit, you can combine it with our classic Marrakech in one day tour.

faq.question: Is it a private tour?
faq.answer: Yes. Your guide and driver are for your group only, and the pace and stops adapt to your interests. There is no minimum group size.

faq.question: Are entrance fees included?
faq.answer: No. Entrance fees for Dar Si Said, the Koubba, Le Jardin Secret and the synagogue are paid on the spot and are usually modest. Bring some dirhams in cash.

faq.question: What is the Mellah?
faq.answer: The Mellah is the old Jewish quarter of Marrakech, founded in the 16th century beside the royal palace. Jewish communities lived here for centuries and played a major role in trade and crafts. Today you can visit the Lazama synagogue, the spice market and one of the largest Jewish cemeteries in Morocco.

faq.question: How much walking is there?
faq.answer: Less than on most city tours. The routes are flat, and your private driver takes you between the more distant sites, such as the Menara gardens. It's a good choice for travellers who prefer a gentler pace.

faq.question: What time does the tour start?
faq.answer: Usually at around 11:00, with pick-up at your hotel or riad, and drop-off at about 17:30. As the tour is private, we can start earlier or later; just tell us when you book.

faq.question: Is lunch included?
faq.answer: No. Your guide recommends a riad restaurant or a local café, depending on your taste and budget. Vegetarian options are easy to find.

faq.question: What makes Le Jardin Secret special?
faq.answer: It's a 19th-century riad garden in the heart of the medina, restored in 2016. It has two gardens, an Islamic garden laid out in four parts around a fountain and an exotic garden with plants from around the world, plus a tower with a view over the medina's rooftops. It's one of the calmest places in the old city.

faq.question: Can we combine this tour with the main sights?
faq.answer: Yes. Many travellers do our Marrakech in one day tour first and this one the next day. We can also make a custom day mixing both, for example the Bahia Palace and the souks in the morning and the Mellah and Le Jardin Secret in the afternoon.

faq.question: Is it suitable for families?
faq.answer: Yes. The routes are flat, the gardens give children space to move, and the car makes breaks easy. Your guide can adapt the stories for children.

faq.question: What should I wear?
faq.answer: Light, comfortable clothes that cover shoulders and knees, especially for the synagogue and the cemetery. Comfortable shoes, sunglasses and a hat are useful.

faq.question: When is the best time for this tour?
faq.answer: All year. Spring and autumn are the most pleasant. In summer, the late start and the shaded gardens and museums make the heat easier to handle. In winter, days are mild and sunny.

faq.question: Will I be taken to shops?
faq.answer: Only if you want to. The tour focuses on history and places, not shopping. If you'd like to buy spices, crafts or textiles, your guide can recommend fair places and help you bargain.
